meta.scope: Published exterior dimensions and control layout for the 12 lenses in data/lenses/*.json. Five lenses are tied to a real product (representativeOf set) and carry that product's own maker-published figures. The other seven are class-representative designs; each gets rounded values derived from 2-3 real lenses of the same focal length and aperture class, cited individually and labeled assumed. See research/exteriors.md for prose, source conflicts, and what could not be found.
meta.schema: Each lens entry: diameterMm, lengthMm, lengthFrom, filterMm, weightG, apertureRing, focusRing, distanceScale, hood -- each an object carrying its own ev/src/loc (or, for an assumed class figure, classSources listing every cited real lens). The 09/28/2026 exterior-pane addendum below (keys s35, n50, n500, n500fl, z35, m50, z800 -- one entry per lens in the PANE.md two-body/three-lens-each lineup) adds three more fields on the same pattern: mount (one of mounts.json's keys), controlRing (Z-mount lenses only: {v, programmable, ev, src, loc, accessed}), tripodCollar (telephotos only: {v, removable, ev, src, loc, accessed}).
openProblems: No source found for where along the barrel the focus ring sits on any of the 12 lenses (front third / middle / near mount). Every focusRing.positionOnBarrel field below is null with a note to derive it from the lens's own focus-group position in data/lenses/*.json instead.
Sony FE 135mm F1.8 GM: no source found stating whether it has a distance scale window; Sony's modern GM primes generally omit one, so distanceScale.v is recorded false but labeled assumed, not spec.

p28 (28mm f/1.8 patent design) sits between two real-lens populations: the one true same-aperture lens found (Canon EF 28mm f/1.8 USM, a small consumer design) and two faster f/1.4 designs of the same focal length (Sigma 28mm F1.4 Art, Nikon 28mm f/1.4E), which are considerably larger. The representative figure is interpolated and flagged low-confidence in its own entry.

p200 (200mm f/2 class) has only two real same-spec anchors (Nikon AF-S 200mm f/2G ED VR II, Canon EF 200mm f/2L IS USM); a third real 200mm f/2 (Sigma 200mm F2 DG OS Sports) exists but is a 2025 mirrorless-native design with no independently found dimension set in this session, so it is not used.

p400/p500 (400mm f/2.8, 500mm f/4 classes): Sony's FE 400mm F2.8 GM OSS diameter and the Nikon 500mm f/4E FL ED VR diameter were not found as text in this session (search results returned only length/weight/filter); each class representative is derived from the two/three lenses that did yield a diameter.

The other two cited lenses are faster 28mm f/1.4 designs (83, 83mm) and are noticeably larger. 80mm interpolates toward the f/1.8 anchor rather than averaging all three straight, since a faster aperture at the same focal length should need more glass diameter than the f/1.8 design and less than the f/1.4 pair. filterMm.loc: Specifications tab, "46mm" rear drop-in filter holder; no front filter thread (the front element is exposed behind a fixed hood mount, standard for this class)

apertureRing.note: No source found stating an aperture ring on this lens; Nikon's current Z super-telephoto S-line primes control aperture from the body/control ring, not a dedicated ring, matching m500/n500 in this file.

focusRing.type: focus-by-wire, stepping-motor AF, internal focus (the front group and the Phase Fresnel element do not move)
focusRing.note: Z-mount S-line convention; internal-focus construction typical of a PF super-telephoto of this size (front group mass makes front-focusing impractical).

distanceScale.note: Same reasoning as z35/m50: current Z-mount S-line primes show focus distance on the camera display, not an engraved barrel window; the research note for this lens found no diaphragm-blade or barrel-window information on Nikon's own spec page either.

hood.model: bayonet hood, integrated lens-hood mount forward of the filter ring (standard for this class)

tripodCollar.loc: product photography shows a built-in rotating tripod collar ring with a removable foot, consistent with every Nikon super-telephoto PF design in this file (n500, m500)

controlRing.loc: product photography and Nikon's Z S-line control-ring convention, applied to every current Z S-line prime; not independently re-confirmed by spec-table text for this specific model this session
